messages:
FinanceOps: Heads up  monthly bill reconciliation shows sustained-use discounts applied to partner account `partner-consumption` instead of our consuming projects. Delta ~ $9,000. Need quick attribution and provisional allocation plan. :thinking:
eng-platform: can you share the billing dataset? I'll run the credits vs usage slice. :mag:
FinanceOps: billing_view.gcp_billing_export_v1_55511. Usual SQL to crosswalk credits:
```sql
SELECT project_id, SUM(cost) AS cost, SUM(credit_amount) AS credits
FROM `billing_view.gcp_billing_export_v1_55511.gcp_billing_export_v1_*`
WHERE invoice_month = '2026-04' AND sku_description LIKE '%GPU%'
GROUP BY project_id
ORDER BY credits DESC;
```
eng-platform: ran it. Top rows: partner-consumption credits $9,000 (usage $0), client-onboarding usage $6,400 credits $0, model-tuning usage $2,100 credits $0. Looks like credits landed on partner project.
lena: partner-consumption was created during the Jan migration and we intended to have credits auto-distributed as sustained-use; maybe the billing account link is set to host instead of consumers.
partner-rep: from vendor side: sustained-use credits are applied to the billing account level unless you supply per-project allocation. During consolidation we pointed the consolidated billing account to `partner-consumption` for legacy reasons. We can request reallocation but vendor will need proof of consumer usage within the invoice period.
FinanceOps: ok. Two parallel actions: (1) provisional internal allocation so teams don't show overspend in April, (2) vendor case to recover or reissue credits if vendor agrees. Can eng-platform compute GPU-hours to prorate provisional allocation?
eng-platform: quick query for GPU hours by project for Apr:
```sql
SELECT project_id, SUM(usage_amount) AS gpu_hours
FROM `billing_view.gcp_billing_export_v1_55511.gcp_billing_export_v1_*`
WHERE invoice_month='2026-04' AND sku_description LIKE '%GPU%'
GROUP BY project_id
ORDER BY gpu_hours DESC;
```
eng-platform: result: client-onboarding 400 GPU-hrs, model-tuning 130 GPU-hrs, infra-test 20 GPU-hrs (we'll ignore infra-test for this allocation if small). Total for major consumers = 530 GPU-hrs.
FinanceOps: credits to allocate = $9,000. Proportional allocation: client-onboarding = round(400/530*9000) = $6,792; model-tuning = $2,208. I'll create provisional ledger transfers and tag them with VND-452 (vendor case).
billing-bot: Ticket created: BILL-3333 "Sustained-use credits misdirected to partner account; provisional reallocation created". Assignee: lena. Due: 7 business days.
partner-rep: I'll open vendor support case VND-452 and attach the BigQuery exports and the invoice. Vendor contact: acme-cloud-billing@vendor.example. They typically respond in 3-5 business days. If they accept, they'll either reapply credits to consumer projects or issue a credit to the billing account which we can reassign.
lena: created ledger entries PROV-ALLOC-2026-04-09 with the two transfers and a note that we'll reverse if vendor reissues. Filing location: finance/shared/2026/04/provisional_allocs.
product-ops: suggestion: add a reservation/credits ownership field to the procurement flow and a post-bill check that flags credits landing on non-consumer projects. We should also add a short-run alert when large credits appear on a host project.
FinanceOps: agreed. I'll add an action item to the April billing retro: add the monitoring rule and require a billing-account owner in the purchase request.
eng-platform: also found a terraform commit that changed billing_account mapping (commit d4f2c9, 2026-01-12). Tagging it in the vendor case to show intent.
FinanceOps: thanks. Closing this thread; follow BILL-3333 and VND-452 for updates. :white_check_mark:
